messages.subject: help working with mapreduce in R with files inside HDFS
parts:
Hi. I would like to ask you for help because I'm out of alternatives and I can't get my example to work.

I have in hdfs a file with weather information per station per date. Something like this:

 {station}     {date}    {windSpeed}  {windDirection}   {windPeakSpeed}

 USW00027502     19970915        106     110     165
 USW00027502     19970926        52      40      80
 USW00027502     19971006        43      110     72

I've tried to create a simple algorith to pick up means and standard deviations, but I have several problems at the moment the information has to be settle as key-value in the map. I have plenty of experience in Hadoop and in MapReduce programming (but in Java), so I'm trying to adapt to this new form. This is my code:

 hdfs.input.path <- '/tmp/wind/windValues.txt'
 hdfs.output.path <- '/tmp/windAggregate'

 col.names <- c('station','date','average','direction','peak')
 data.input.format = make.input.format('
                csv',
                'text',
                sep='\t',
                col.names=col.names,
                stringsAsFactors=F)
 
 mapper.aggregates <- function(k, fields) {
         # k is comming as NULL, so I put the value of the first column in fields.
         k <- fields$station
         # rmr.str(k)
         # rmr.str(fields)
         keyval(k,list(fields$average, fields$direction, fields$peak))
 }
 
 reducer.aggregater <- function(k, value.list) {
    # rmr.str(k)
    # rmr.str(value.list)
    if(require(plyr))
        value.df <- ldply(value.list, as.numeric)
    else {
        value.list <- lapply(value.list, as.numeric)
        value.df <- data.frame( do.call(rbind, value.list))
    }    
    # rmr.str(value.df)
    colnames(value.df) <- c('average', 'direction', 'peak')
    if(length(value.df$average) > 10) {
        avg <- mean(value.df$average)
        sdA <- sd(value.df$average)
        sdD <- sd(value.df$direction)
        maxP <- max(value.df$peak)
        keyval(k, c(avg,sdA,sdD,maxP))
    }    
 }

 mr.aggregate.wind <- function(input, output) {
      mapreduce(input=input,
          output=output,
          input.format=data.input.format,
          map = mapper.aggregates,
          reduce = reducer.aggregater
          )
 }
 

and the call to the operation: 
  df <- from.dfs(mr.aggregate.wind(hdfs.input.path, hdfs.output.path))

My problem seems to be that I can get the proper value inside the mapper, it seems that a full vector of integer is generated in the keyvalue (I think because I use c( ) for different vectors, generating a concatenation of all of them). So the reducer receives a vector of integers, instead of a list. If I try to generate a list with keyvalue(k, list(v$1, v$2....) I get a Broken Pipe error within the mapper, and the sterr doesn't have more information related to the error.

Another think I am having difficulties is with this new paradigm. When I debugged fields within the map, I was surprised the fields is a dataframe with vectors for every field. I am used to the M/R paradigm, where every map operation receives only one line. and here it seems that it receives a full list. Is guaranteed that there will be only one key for the first column of the values? How I have to work with this? Here is the example of my debug:

messages.author: 63023c771a070260
messages.subject: Re: help working with mapreduce in R with files inside HDFS
parts:
Hi,
R doesn't have scalar values and doesn't support scalar computation very well. So the idea is that every function should manipulate vectors, lists or some collection. So the same is true here. Map will take two collections as arguments (keys and values) and match them positionally. They can be vectors, lists, matrices or data frames. When the collection has two dimensions, the second one is considered dominant (each row of a matrix or data frame becomes a key or value, logically). The same is true for the keyval function, it is vectorized and the same conventions apply. So when I see in your code

 keyval(k,list(fields$average, fields$direction, fields$peak))

I am almost sure it is  a mistake because you value argument is a list of three elements which will become three separate records. What you meant was probably

 keyval(k,data.frame(fields$average, fields$direction, fields$peak))


Now we have a vector as key arg and a data frame with the same number of rows as the vector k, and everything should match nicely. I would be happy to agree that this is not documented because then I could just go and fix that, unfortunately this is in help(mapreduce) and helpl(keyval) so the problem is for me to write more clearly or to force people to read what I write, both unsolved problems. I think you are taking the right approach to start with a small data set and put some rmr.str statements to understand what is going on, even better you could switch to the local backend and step through the map and reduce. I am sure that if you fix your map function things will start to make sense. I am not sure I understand your question about the grouping for one key, but the general answer is that grouping is taken care of for you so unless you use the vectorized reduce option there will be a single reduce call for each distinct key. I would suggest, comment out the reduce argument for now and run a map only job with the correction I suggested and see if that makes sense, then turn on the reduce. If it doesn't get better, please report back here.


Antonio
